why: The target claim C1 is produced entirely by the CRAN R package otsfeatures released by the authors. The package bundles SyntheticData2 and implements c_marginal_probabilities, c_joint_probabilities, and the paper's clustering/validation workflow. No author repository is needed; the only work is installing R plus CRAN dependencies and running the documented snippet. The computation is tiny and CPU-only.
entrypoints: CRAN package otsfeatures: library(otsfeatures); SyntheticData2$data; c_marginal_probabilities(states=0:5); c_joint_probabilities(states=0:5, lag=1); c_joint_probabilities(states=0:5, lag=2); dist(dataset_1); ClusterR::pam(k=4); ClusterR::external_validation(...)
blockers_seen: R runtime is not confirmed installed on this Windows machine; R and CRAN dependencies such as ClusterR must be installed.
No GitHub repository is provided, but the CRAN package source is the authors' released implementation.

feasibility.est_runtime_on_this_machine: About 5-10 minutes total: install R/CRAN dependencies, download otsfeatures, build the 80x55 cumulative-feature matrix, run dist + PAM(k=4), and compute ARI. The actual clustering is well under 1 minute.

compute.basis: An 80-series synthetic dataset is reduced to a 55-column feature matrix; distance computation and PAM with k=4 are negligible, so nearly all command time is R/package installation.
